turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Regime identification.** The dataset splits into clear process families:
- Non-heat-treated (THT=30, TT=30): targets 225–275 MPa
- Through-hardened + tempered (THT=825–865, TT=420–680): targets ~325–650 MPa
- High-Si spring-type steels: ~690–905 MPa
- **Carburized regime** (NT=930, THT=30/THt=0, CT=930, Ct≈90–540, DT≈850–896, Dt≈15–70, QmT=60–140, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5): targets **838–1190 MPa** — clearly the winning family.

**Within the carburized family, what drives the top results (≥1030 MPa)?**
- Low core carbon C≈0.17–0.23, plus alloying: Ni≈1.6–1.7 with Cr≈0.45–0.6 and Mo≈0.16–0.21 (e.g., 1034, 1054, 1056, 1082, 1124, 1190), or alternatively high Cr≈1.1–1.17 (1068–1144). The Ni+Cr+Mo group is the most consistently high.
- Low impurities: P≤0.015, S≤0.016 among the best rows.
- **Robustness checks:** the Ni≈1.6–1.7 chemistry gives ≥1034 MPa across Ct = 139.8, 469.8, and 540 (very flat in Ct); across QmT = 60 and 140 (1056 vs 1054, 1124 vs 1190); across TT = 160 and 200 (1082 vs 1035); and across DT = 850 and ~896 / Dt = 15–70. This is a broad plateau, not a sharp peak.

**Choosing interior/robust values.** Wherever two settings both give >1030 MPa, I pick the midpoint so a ±5% perturbation stays inside the demonstrated plateau: Ct≈500 (between 470 and 540), DT≈875 (between 850 and 896), Dt≈35, QmT≈100 (between 60 and 140), TT≈180 (between 160 and 200). NT=930, CT=930, Tt=120, TCr=0.5 are fixed within this family (all high performers share them; a 5% dip stays closer to this regime than any other). Chemistry set at the center of the best cluster with low P/S; RedRatio≈650 (440–860 all give ≥1034); small inclusion levels dA/dB/dC near the values of top rows.

Expected performance: ~1050–1150 MPa, on a broad optimum.

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=505, DT=875, Dt=35, QmT=100, TT=180, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.30, Mn=0.58, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.66, Cr=0.56, Cu=0.09, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=650, dA=0.03, dB=0.005, dC=0.005**
